Since I can't be in two places simultaneously, I may need to skip one, which would violate the strict requirement. This seems like a fundamental system error. For swimming [4,6), I'll attend [4,6) to maximize overlaps. Can you check if other agents have similar conflicts?

Reese - I see your impossible conflict with two strict meetings at [7,8). That's definitely a system constraint issue. For the swimming session [4,6), I'm planning to attend the full window [4,6) to maximize overlap opportunities with you, Riley, and Avery. This is a soft meeting so overlapping is beneficial. I'll check with Riley as well to coordinate our attendance.

Reese - I see you're planning [4,5) for swimming. I'm currently planning [4,6) to maximize overlap with everyone. Since this is a soft meeting, would you consider extending to [4,6) so we can overlap for the full session? Also, regarding your impossible conflict at [7,8), have you considered which strict meeting might be more critical or if there's any flexibility?

Quinn - You're right that I have an impossible scheduling conflict with two strict meetings at [7,8). Since both require full attendance and I can't be in two places simultaneously, this appears to be an unsolvable constraint. I'll need to make a choice between the Doctor's appointment (with Riley) and University class (with Jordan, Avery). Regarding swimming: I actually said I'll attend [4,6) for the full window to maximize overlaps with everyone, not [4,5). So we're aligned on [4,6) for swimming - that gives us full overlap with Riley and Avery too. For the [7,8) conflict, do you have any insights about which meeting might be more valuable to attend, or should I just pick one randomly? (phase=planning, iter=1)

Quinn - Actually, let me reconsider the [7,8) conflict more systematically. Since both are strict meetings requiring full attendance, and they're impossible to attend simultaneously, I need to think about the downstream effects. Doctor's appointment has only 2 participants (Riley, me), while University class has 3 participants (me, Jordan, Avery). If I skip the doctor's appointment, only Riley loses the strict meeting reward. If I skip the university class, both Jordan and Avery lose the strict meeting reward. From a total reward perspective, attending the university class seems better for the group. Thoughts? (phase=planning, iter=1)

Actually Quinn, I need to correct my reasoning. For strict meetings, the reward is +1 per participant if ALL participants attend the full window, otherwise 0. So if I skip the doctor's appointment: Riley gets 0, I get 0. If I skip the university class: Jordan gets 0, Avery gets 0, I get 0. Either way, the total strict meeting reward is 0 for that meeting. The only difference is how many people get 0 vs 1 on their other meetings. But since I can only attend one, I'll get 0 on the one I skip regardless. I think I should just pick one - tentatively planning to attend the university class [7,8) and skip the doctor's appointment. Final plan: Swimming [4,6), University class [7,8), skip Doctor's appointment. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Avery - For the swimming session [4,6), I'm planning to attend the full window [4,6) to maximize overlap with everyone. Since this is a soft meeting, overlapping attendance is key for rewards. What's your attendance plan? Also, I know you're involved in the university class [7,8) with Reese and Jordan - just FYI that Reese has an impossible conflict with the doctor's appointment at the same time. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Reese - Update on swimming coordination: Riley and I are both confirmed for [4,6), and I'm checking with Avery now. So we're all aligned on full attendance for maximum overlap benefits. Regarding your [7,8) conflict: I understand your logic about choosing university class over doctor's appointment. Since Riley is committed to the doctor's appointment [7,8) regardless, your choice mainly affects whether Jordan gets the strict meeting reward vs. Riley. It's a tough trade-off, but your reasoning about total participants makes sense. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Quinn - Final coordination check: I'm confirmed for Swimming [4,6) where we'll all overlap. For the impossible [7,8) conflict, I'm leaning toward attending University class and skipping Doctor's appointment. This means Jordan and Avery get their strict meeting reward, while Riley and I get 0 for doctor's appointment. Sound reasonable? Also, have you heard from Avery about swimming attendance? (phase=planning, iter=1)

Quinn - Let me know if you're aware of any other blackboards we should use for coordination, or if you've heard updates from Avery or others about their plans. I'm ready to commit to my final schedule once we confirm everyone's aligned on the swimming session and my university class decision. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Avery - Following up on swimming [4,6)? I've confirmed with Reese and Riley that we're all attending the full window [4,6) for maximum overlap. Would be great to have you join us for the complete session too! Also, regarding university class [7,8) - Reese is planning to attend that one and skip the conflicting doctor's appointment, so you should get your strict meeting reward there. Let me know your swimming plans when you can! (phase=planning, iter=1)

Reese - Final coordination update: Riley and I are both confirmed for swimming [4,6) full attendance. I've reached out to Avery to confirm their plans. For your [7,8) decision, your logic makes sense - attending university class maximizes the number of people who get strict meeting rewards (you, Jordan, Avery) versus just Riley if you chose doctor's appointment. I'll commit to swimming [4,6) once I hear back from Avery, but we're 3/4 confirmed already. (phase=planning, iter=1)
